children: A bond selloff pushed the 2-year Treasury yield Friday to 4.741%, its highest level since July 2024, when the Fed was on the verge of cutting rates for the first time since the post-Covid inflationary shock.

This time around, with inflation still elevated, the prospect of more Fed hikes is pushing short-term yields higher. Though the central bank hiked rates Wednesday, futures markets imply a roughly 90% chance of at least one more quarter-point hike by year end.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
